_about: GM plan and position. Never rendered. Prose for beats, quests and roads lives in saga/bible/_gm/arc.md (saga.py arc <id>); this file holds state. Edit through saga.py plan where a command exists; otherwise with Edit, keeping the canonical format (saga.py fmt).
book_question: Who is hollowing the wounded, and can a knight who cannot stand protect anyone?

chapter.question: What is under the House, and who will take him down to it?

slots.plan: The dawn after the eve (arc b1.3, its run-up). The kitchen's flour at the undercroft door is read at the dawn bell before the House can crowd it: no print in it, and none going out, but a fan of frost glazed on the flour from the gap, as if something below had breathed on it all night; Sister Pell rang every hour with her eye on the door and heard nothing. The cold comes up nightly, and it comes up alone. The House, which believed him last night, now wants the door opened and wants it today, and Darrow is the one man in the hall who cannot go down it. The open climax choice (how the stair is taken) is not resolved here; the scene may lean toward it. Maelis reads the knee in the morning and says nothing about stairs.
slots.turn: By the end the House knows the cold comes up every night, alone, and Darrow must decide how the stair is taken while the whole hall waits on him; he attempts to read the flour before anyone else steps in it, and to keep the House from the door without the Prior's word

slots.plan: The stair on Maelis's terms (ch02 choice, option 1): the second day of asking. He asks again at the hour reading, as she told him to; she answers each question with a sharper one and charges for every answer (what did the knee do this morning; what would you do at the bottom; who carries you up), and he answers them truly. She has not said yes. Wren practises being a shoulder and keeps a count of it. In every shape the one condition no one argues is the Mender's: not until the leg will bear him on a stair.
slots.turn: By the end the stair has its terms (whose leave, whose count, whose key) and Maelis has set the one condition nobody argues, the leg first; Darrow attempts to get the door opened before the leg is ready, and is refused by the one person he will not go against

slots.plan: q1.letters compressed (stages 2 and 3, arc q1.letters): at the hour bell Marrant comes up to the bars himself with two letters in blue wax and hands them through, courteous, as if he were the House's carrier. The second: 'Did you turn? Tell me you did not turn toward the boy.' The third, folded inside it: 'Answer me, or I will come myself.' The second is dated before the list was read at Coldmere: Aldric has known where he is all along. Marrant thanks him for taking them, and asks nothing about the undercroft, which he has not heard of. Ends on the micro. Hollis, from the gatehouse post or the Grey Cot, sees the blue wax a second time and looks away (T3 plant).
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows his oldest friend has known where he lay since before the list, and must answer him, burn him, or keep him; he attempts to take the letters from the Confessor's hand without giving the Confessor his face

micro.ask: What does Darrow do with his brother's letters?
options: Write back as a brother: he will not kneel, and why
Keep them sealed, under the mattress

slots.plan: Opens with Wren on the gate wall with Pell's glass reporting riders on the Holloway, far down, under a banner that is not grey (q1.letters stage 3's end; the riders do not arrive this chapter). Then the leg's first stair since the river, now that it bears him (Knot III): the nine steps down to the warming room off the cloister, with a hand on the wall and Maelis counting, 'every step down is a negotiation', and nine back up; it costs him nothing but his pride and gives him the undercroft. The stair is texture, never a stake.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow has gone down a stair and come back up it on his own leg, and the undercroft is a thing he can do, not a thing he is carried to; the riders give the week a clock; he attempts the nine steps without the hand on the wall, and Maelis puts it back

slots.plan: q1.cart compressed (stages 2 and 3, arc q1.cart): the cage comes up light, a load the grey cloaks have 'inspected'; Rae and Wren on the rope at the top, Rae's palms showing what the rope has done to them. Unasked, Rae says what the almoner's satchel weighed going down last week and what it weighed coming up (b1.2's clue; nobody knows yet what it means). Then the only thing she has ever brought up the mountain that was not on a manifest: the grey mare is alive, lame, a Holloway dealer's, and can be had for the dealer's debt (thread 15). Ends on the micro. The dusk bell catches her at the top and the House keeps her as a guest; on the gate wall at night, the camp's fires below, she tells him at last about the cold in her cart: a crate she once carried to Calden's lower door that froze her cart-bed in midsummer; she does not know what was in it, and she asks him nothing.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows the grey mare lives and must say what he will send down for her, and has Rae's cold at last without knowing what it means; he attempts to keep his face for the mare in front of Wren

micro.ask: The mare can be had for the dealer's debt. What does Darrow send down?
options: His name, as surety: a captain's word, though the Faithless have no credit in the Lowmarch
Word, through Rae, that the mare is wanted for the House's stables, in Mother Ione's name
Nothing. Leave her where she is

slots.plan: The eve of the descent (option 1). Maelis's first unforced yes, on her terms, given in her own words and not as a bargain; she will come down behind them without a lamp and does not say how she knows the way (T8 plant). The door is still the Prior's: Darrow goes to Mother Ione with the answer to her question at the door (what he would do at the bottom of the stair: come back up it, on his own leg, at the Mender's count), and she says she will open it at dusk tomorrow. Hollis, told, asks to be carried to the stair's head; he cannot go down, and he will not be left at the Grey Cot for this. Something to take down: a lamp, oilcloth, a pry bar from the kitchen, chosen by whoever is careful.
slots.turn: By the end the descent is set for tomorrow, with its terms and its people, and Hollis has made himself part of it from the top of the stair; Darrow attempts to go tonight and is held to the morning by the terms he agreed

slots.plan: The stair (arc b1.3, plants; option 1). The Prior opens the door at dusk with the key from her neck; Wren goes first with the lamp and his hand on her shoulder, Maelis behind them without a lamp, counting; Hollis's voice from the top telling him to look at the wall and not the floor; step by step, the knee bearing him. At the bottom a hall older than the House: Wren reads the words cut over the inner door aloud before Maelis can translate them and stops herself halfway (T6); they pass a door with script round its frame and no handle, where Maelis's hand rests a moment too long (q1.door). The walls are painted. Ends with the lamp on the far wall, where frost is spreading across the stone from a low alcove beneath where the infirmary floor must be: the climax is what is in it.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow has gone down the stair on his own leg into a hall nobody living walks but one, and sees the frost on the far wall; he attempts the stair under the terms the choice set, and keeps them

world_moves: the grey cloaks built a stone windbreak on the lower terrace and roofed it with the camp's cart-canvas: they mean to winter
a lymer came up to the Confessors' camp from the valley; its baying comes up the Steps after dark and the House's kennel answers it
the first hard frost took the last herbs in the cloister garden, and the kitchen opened the winter stores a week early

climax.plan: What is under the House (arc b1.3). The alcove beneath the infirmary floor, the frost spreading from it, and in it a sliver of the same black stone as the chip under Benedek's tongue, set in mortar that is new, laid since the first snow, in a hole the width of a letter-satchel; the cold drawing up through the floor toward the wounded above (`shard_found`). The murals around them: the Reckoning, and among them a kneeling knight with light running up out of him along a thread (T7 plant; a new thread). By tier: Triumph, Darrow reads the murals aloud as far as the Reckoning lets him and brings the shard up wrapped in oilcloth, the frost burning through to his hands, and on the far cots the Hollowed turn their heads to follow it; Hard-won, the shard is too cold to lift and stays, but he has seen it and the fresh mortar, and that is enough to know it was carried; Costly, the shard is gone when they come back with the lamp and Maelis, the mortar still wet: someone in the House moved it between dusk and dawn; Setback, the alcove is empty and newly broken, and at dusk Marrant announces at the bars that he will inspect the undercroft for witchery under his writ. Hollis waits at the stair's head and is the first face when they come up. The knee is never the stake: the stair back up is texture. Ends on the choice: who is told.
checks: insight DC 13 (Warden's Eye: the mortar's age, the murals, what was carried and how)
vigor DC 13 (holding the cold of the stone long enough: the frost into his hands)
finesse DC 12 (freeing the shard from the mortar without breaking it)
options: Tell the Prior everything, shard and murals
Tell Hollis and the far cots' keepers first, and the Prior only after: his own people before the House's law
Tell no one yet, and watch the stair

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.
